source_conflicts.resolution: Tests p2 specifies every 60 days; complications p6 specifies monthly. Preserve both with local-team reconciliation rather than silently choose a universal interval.
Table 5 says RPED Table 5 below; the actual RPED table is Table 6 on p6. Audit references Table 6.

indications.description: Adult patients with unresectable or metastatic melanoma with a confirmed BRAF V600 mutation.
Adjuvant treatment following complete resection of stage III BRAF V600-mutated melanoma.

treatment.schedule_summary: Dabrafenib 150 mg twice daily plus trametinib 2 mg once daily, continuously. A 28-day assessment convention does not create a break. Advanced melanoma: until progression/unacceptable toxicity. Completely resected Stage III adjuvant melanoma: 12 months unless recurrence/unacceptable toxicity.
treatment.cycle_convention_note: Continuous daily oral treatment. 28 days is an administrative assessment convention, not a drug-free interval.
treatment.administration: Swallow whole with water 1 hour before or 2 hours after food. Do not crush, chew or mix with food/liquids. Take trametinib with the morning or evening dabrafenib dose at the same time daily. Missed dabrafenib: only take if >6 hours to the next dose; trametinib: only if >12 hours. Do not replace a vomited trametinib dose.
treatment.dose_reduction_reference: Dabrafenib 150 →100 →75 →50 mg twice daily; trametinib 2 →1.5 →1 →1 mg daily. Lower doses are not recommended in this combination. Confirm actual dose history; no automatic dose calculation.

rules.explanation: No renal dose adjustment is required for mild/moderate impairment. Preserve other reductions and clinical monitoring.

rules.explanation: No hepatic dose adjustment is required for mild impairment; retain other restrictions.

action.message: Dabrafenib was not studied at creatinine >1.5 ×ULN. Monitor renal function; rising creatinine may require dabrafenib interruption as clinically appropriate, without an invented fixed dose.

rules.explanation: Dabrafenib was not studied at creatinine >1.5 ×ULN. Monitor renal function; rising creatinine may require dabrafenib interruption as clinically appropriate, without an invented fixed dose.

action.message: For other Grade 1 or tolerable Grade 2 events, continue and monitor. Specific organ exceptions and all other restrictions still apply.

rules.explanation: For other Grade 1 or tolerable Grade 2 events, continue and monitor. Specific organ exceptions and all other restrictions still apply.

action.message: Grade 2 requires confirmation of tolerability; intolerable events require interruption.

rules.explanation: Grade 2 requires confirmation of tolerability; intolerable events require interruption.

action.message: Interrupt both medicines until Grade 0–1; then consider a one-level reduction from each actual current dose with the consultant.

rules.explanation: Interrupt both medicines until Grade 0–1; then consider a one-level reduction from each actual current dose with the consultant.

action.message: Grade 4: permanently discontinue OR interrupt until Grade 0–1 and resume one level lower. This is an explicit consultant choice; no automatic restart or compulsory permanent stop is inferred.

rules.explanation: Grade 4: permanently discontinue OR interrupt until Grade 0–1 and resume one level lower. This is an explicit consultant choice; no automatic restart or compulsory permanent stop is inferred.

action.message: Review the peak grade and intolerability, recovery to Grade 0–1 and prior dose levels. Grade 4 retains the permanent-stop alternative. Do not automatically apply a second reduction to the same episode.

rules.explanation: Review the peak grade and intolerability, recovery to Grade 0–1 and prior dose levels. Grade 4 retains the permanent-stop alternative. Do not automatically apply a second reduction to the same episode.

action.message: Interrupt BOTH dabrafenib and trametinib for temperature ≥38°C, or at the first symptom of recurrent pyrexia. Assess infection, hydration, blood pressure and renal function; use prescribed antipyretics and consider corticosteroids only if insufficient.

rules.explanation: Interrupt BOTH dabrafenib and trametinib for temperature ≥38°C, or at the first symptom of recurrent pyrexia. Assess infection, hydration, blood pressure and renal function; use prescribed antipyretics and consider corticosteroids only if insufficient.

action.message: Do not restart until completely symptom-free for at least 24 hours. Missing duration is not evidence of recovery.

rules.explanation: Do not restart until completely symptom-free for at least 24 hours. Missing duration is not evidence of recovery.

action.message: The ≥24-hour symptom-free criterion is met. Confirm recovery and actual doses; same-level restart or one-level reduction for recurrent/severe fever remains a clinician decision, not automatic clearance.

rules.explanation: The ≥24-hour symptom-free criterion is met. Confirm recovery and actual doses; same-level restart or one-level reduction for recurrent/severe fever remains a clinician decision, not automatic clearance.

action.message: Recurrent pyrexia or associated severe dehydration, hypotension or renal failure supports considering a one-level reduction once symptom-free ≥24 hours.

rules.explanation: Recurrent pyrexia or associated severe dehydration, hypotension or renal failure supports considering a one-level reduction once symptom-free ≥24 hours.

action.message: Effective local ocular treatment permits no dabrafenib dose reduction for uveitis; trametinib needs no modification for this exception.

rules.explanation: Effective local ocular treatment permits no dabrafenib dose reduction for uveitis; trametinib needs no modification for this exception.

action.message: Withhold dabrafenib until ocular inflammation resolves, then restart one level lower. No trametinib modification is required solely for this exception.

rules.explanation: Withhold dabrafenib until ocular inflammation resolves, then restart one level lower. No trametinib modification is required solely for this exception.

action.message: Confirm whether local ocular treatment controls uveitis before choosing the dabrafenib pathway.

rules.explanation: Confirm whether local ocular treatment controls uveitis before choosing the dabrafenib pathway.

action.message: After dabrafenib interruption for refractory uveitis, confirm complete ocular-inflammation resolution and restart one level below the actual prior dose; trametinib is unchanged by this exception.

rules.explanation: After dabrafenib interruption for refractory uveitis, confirm complete ocular-inflammation resolution and restart one level below the actual prior dose; trametinib is unchanged by this exception.

action.message: Interrupt trametinib for an absolute LVEF fall >10 percentage points AND below institutional LLN. Assess symptoms/grade and recovery; dabrafenib requires no change for this exception.

rules.explanation: Interrupt trametinib for an absolute LVEF fall >10 percentage points AND below institutional LLN. Assess symptoms/grade and recovery; dabrafenib requires no change for this exception.

action.message: Permanently discontinue trametinib for Grade 3–4 LVD or clinician-confirmed LVEF non-recovery. No source time limit is invented. Dabrafenib is unchanged by this exception.

rules.explanation: Permanently discontinue trametinib for Grade 3–4 LVD or clinician-confirmed LVEF non-recovery. No source time limit is invented. Dabrafenib is unchanged by this exception.

action.message: Interrupt trametinib pending urgent cardiac assessment and grading; Grade 3–4 or non-recovery mandates permanent discontinuation. The asymptomatic pathway is not enough for symptomatic disease.

rules.explanation: Interrupt trametinib pending urgent cardiac assessment and grading; Grade 3–4 or non-recovery mandates permanent discontinuation. The asymptomatic pathway is not enough for symptomatic disease.

action.message: After verified LVEF recovery, trametinib may restart one dose level lower with careful monitoring. The source does not define a fixed recovery duration; confirm the individual cardiac decision.

rules.explanation: After verified LVEF recovery, trametinib may restart one dose level lower with careful monitoring. The source does not define a fixed recovery duration; confirm the individual cardiac decision.

action.message: Permanently discontinue trametinib for diagnosed RVO. Dabrafenib needs no modification solely for this exception.

rules.explanation: Permanently discontinue trametinib for diagnosed RVO. Dabrafenib needs no modification solely for this exception.

action.message: Grade 1 RPED: continue trametinib with monthly retinal evaluation until resolution. Worsening requires the hold pathway.

rules.explanation: Grade 1 RPED: continue trametinib with monthly retinal evaluation until resolution. Worsening requires the hold pathway.

action.message: Withhold trametinib for up to 3 weeks for Grade 2–3 RPED or worsening Grade 1. Use ophthalmic reassessment and the recovery pathway; dabrafenib is unchanged.

rules.explanation: Withhold trametinib for up to 3 weeks for Grade 2–3 RPED or worsening Grade 1. Use ophthalmic reassessment and the recovery pathway; dabrafenib is unchanged.

action.message: Grade 2–3 RPED improved to Grade 0–1 within 3 weeks: consider restarting trametinib 0.5 mg below the actual previous dose; do not calculate without pharmacy verification.

rules.explanation: Grade 2–3 RPED improved to Grade 0–1 within 3 weeks: consider restarting trametinib 0.5 mg below the actual previous dose; do not calculate without pharmacy verification.

action.message: When Grade 2–3 RPED recovers within 3 weeks in a patient already taking trametinib 1 mg daily, discontinue trametinib rather than reduce below the source minimum.

rules.explanation: When Grade 2–3 RPED recovers within 3 weeks in a patient already taking trametinib 1 mg daily, discontinue trametinib rather than reduce below the source minimum.

action.message: Permanently discontinue trametinib if Grade 2–3 RPED has not improved to at least Grade 1 within 3 weeks.

rules.explanation: Permanently discontinue trametinib if Grade 2–3 RPED has not improved to at least Grade 1 within 3 weeks.

action.message: Urgent ophthalmic/consultant review. The RPED-specific table covers Grades 1–3; do not invent a Grade 4 restart dose. Reconcile the generic Grade 4 and specific ocular pathways.

rules.explanation: Urgent ophthalmic/consultant review. The RPED-specific table covers Grades 1–3; do not invent a Grade 4 restart dose. Reconcile the generic Grade 4 and specific ocular pathways.

action.message: Withhold trametinib for suspected ILD/pneumonitis pending investigation. Dabrafenib is not automatically modified by this source exception.

rules.explanation: Withhold trametinib for suspected ILD/pneumonitis pending investigation. Dabrafenib is not automatically modified by this source exception.

action.message: Permanently discontinue trametinib for confirmed treatment-related ILD/pneumonitis. Dabrafenib is unchanged by this exception.

rules.explanation: Permanently discontinue trametinib for confirmed treatment-related ILD/pneumonitis. Dabrafenib is unchanged by this exception.

action.message: Withdraw both medicines and urgently assess possible SJS/DRESS or another severe cutaneous adverse reaction. Do not route suspected SCAR through an ordinary tolerable-rash pathway.

rules.explanation: Withdraw both medicines and urgently assess possible SJS/DRESS or another severe cutaneous adverse reaction. Do not route suspected SCAR through an ordinary tolerable-rash pathway.

action.message: Promptly investigate unexplained abdominal pain, including amylase/lipase. Closely monitor any dabrafenib restart after pancreatitis; no fixed reduction is specified.

rules.explanation: Promptly investigate unexplained abdominal pain, including amylase/lipase. Closely monitor any dabrafenib restart after pancreatitis; no fixed reduction is specified.

action.message: Review diverticulitis, GI metastases and interacting medicines that increase perforation risk; use trametinib with caution.

rules.explanation: Review diverticulitis, GI metastases and interacting medicines that increase perforation risk; use trametinib with caution.

action.message: Urgently assess clinically significant bleeding, grade it and apply the source Grade 3/4 and specific pathways. No universal permanent-stop rule is supplied.

rules.explanation: Urgently assess clinically significant bleeding, grade it and apply the source Grade 3/4 and specific pathways. No universal permanent-stop rule is supplied.

action.message: Re-escalation may be considered only after effective adverse-event management, through the same steps, never above dabrafenib 150 mg twice daily or trametinib 2 mg daily; preserve organ-specific exceptions.

rules.explanation: Re-escalation may be considered only after effective adverse-event management, through the same steps, never above dabrafenib 150 mg twice daily or trametinib 2 mg daily; preserve organ-specific exceptions.

action.message: Confirm whether Grade 1 RPED is stable or worsening; stable disease permits monthly retinal review, whereas worsening requires a trametinib hold.

rules.explanation: Confirm whether Grade 1 RPED is stable or worsening; stable disease permits monthly retinal review, whereas worsening requires a trametinib hold.

eligibility: Source-supported advanced or completely resected Stage III adjuvant melanoma
Baseline LVEF at or above institutional LLN
exclusions: Advanced-pathway treatment failure with prior BRAF/MEK inhibitor; intolerance switching is distinct

supportive_care.mapping_basis: NCCP 00415 v5 p6: dabrafenib moderate-to-high; trametinib minimal-to-low. Use local oral antiemetic policy.
supportive_care.supportive_medications_label: NCCP antiemetic guidance for oral SACT
other_supportive_care: No specific routine supportive medicine is mandated by the regimen; apply local antiemetic and symptom protocols.
Pyrexia: clinician-directed antipyretics; consider oral corticosteroids if insufficient.
Alternative effective contraception during treatment, for 2 weeks after dabrafenib and 16 weeks after the last trametinib dose in this combination; hormonal contraception may be less effective.
Discuss fertility preservation; impaired spermatogenesis may be irreversible.

baseline: Dermatologic evaluation for other skin cancer
Review head/neck and non-cutaneous malignancy surveillance
during: FBC, renal and liver profile monthly
ECG and echocardiogram after the first 4 weeks, then every 12 weeks and after dose modification; confirm individual cycle timing
Skin surveillance: tests section says every 60 days; complication section says monthly. Confirm local dermatology schedule
Head/neck examination every 3 months; chest CT every 6 months in the tests section; broader chest/abdomen surveillance is described in complications
Review visual symptoms; creatinine, pancreatitis and other investigations when indicated
after: Skin and non-cutaneous malignancy surveillance up to 6 months after stopping or until another antineoplastic therapy, according to the source and individual plan
monitoring.disease_monitoring: Individual consultant plan; no universal tumour-marker panel or response-imaging interval is specified.
